correctness.rationale: For the exact n-bit digital offsets in arXiv:2610.23363v1 Lemma 2.1, integer-floor algebra gives independent column-bit coefficients e_i=(b_i−x_i)/2; these have known sign, so their positive and negative extrema are exact. Their sum s/N≥0 proves the absolute maximum is the bit-reversal positive extremum. A two-branch induction solves the Bellman equation V_m(x), with recurrences u_m=1−u_{m−1}/2 and a_m=a_{m−1}+(1−u_{m−1})/2 and verified base values; the solution a_n gives the claimed sharp bound, attained by optimal binary actions. All quantifiers n≥1, s,t∈[0,2^n) hold. Independent exact rational brute-force for all columns n≤7 and per-slope checks n≤11 corroborate but do not establish the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The 2026 numerical Hough comparison identifies accurate sampling and comparability of geometric error as meaningful for dyadic Radon implementations; Rim gives only n/2 for its s/N slope. A sharp n/6+O(1) row-tube constant is a factor-three asymptotic reduction of the safe geometric bound, while the explicit per-slope formula and bit-reversal witness make tolerances precisely computable and verifiable in O(n) per slope. No unsupported inverse accuracy improvement is asserted.
